negative_findings.description: Albanian-language queries aimed at law-firm alerts ('njoftim ligjor', 'buletin ligjor', 'ndryshimet në ligjin bankar', 'analizë avokat') returned almost exclusively primary sources (Gazeta Zyrtare, BQK PDFs, ATK presentations, Kuvendi) and NGO/think-tank analyses (GAP Institute, KCSF, IKD), not law-firm client alerts.
negative_findings.result_summary: No Kosovo law firm was found publishing a dated banking/payments legal alert in Albanian; the firms that do publish (RPHS, Vokshi & Lata) do so in English.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: It means the 'summarised before an English version exists' assumption of this cell is inverted for Kosovo: the firm layer is English-first, and the Albanian-first layer is regulators plus NGOs. Local-language monitoring for this cell should target regulator and NGO outputs, not firm newsletters.

negative_findings.description: No Serbian-language (sr) professional-interpreter source for Kosovo banking/payments regulation was located in this run; searches were executed in sq and en, and Serbian-language legal-advisory content addressing Kosovo (XK) regulation did not surface via the queries used.
negative_findings.result_summary: Zero sr-language law-firm or advisory alert sources identified for this cell.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Serbian-language coverage of Kosovo financial regulation is a stated run requirement; leaving it empty risks missing the northern-Kosovo/Serbia-facing advisory layer, which may interpret CBK rules differently.

negative_findings.description: For KPMG and EY, only office/overview pages were confirmed; the specific Kosovo tax & legal alert index URL was not observed. Deloitte's Kosovo alerts sit on the Albania (www2.deloitte.com/al) hub which is mid-migration to deloitte.com/ce, so the listing URL may redirect.
negative_findings.result_summary: PwC Kosovo has an explicit Tax News page; Deloitte has a confirmed Albania/Kosova alert index (possibly moving); KPMG and EY Kosovo alert indexes remain unlocated.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Without stable index URLs the crawler cannot reliably detect new alerts; a manual triage pass is needed before scheduling collection.

brief: Kosovo's professional-interpreter layer for banking and payments rules is small, English-first, and concentrated in two clusters: a handful of Prishtina corporate firms (RPHS Law is the standout, with dated posts on the new Law on Banks, crypto-asset licensing and the SEPA legislative package; plus Vokshi & Lata, Sejdiu & Qerkini and the regional Boga/Kalo desks) and the Big Four tax practices (PwC Kosovo has an explicit Kosovo Tax News page; Deloitte Kosova publishes via the Albania/Kosova alert hub and has covered the CBK electronic payment instruments regulation and Fiscal Package 2.0; KPMG and EY serve Kosovo from Pristina offices but their Kosovo alert indexes were not pinned down). Aggregators — CEE Legal Matters' Kosovo section and Lexology — are the most efficient pointers, because they surface firm-authored briefings that never get indexed well on the firms' own sites. The important negative result is that Albanian-language querying produced regulators, the Official Gazette, ATK presentations and NGO analyses rather than law-firm alerts, and no Serbian-language interpreter source was found at all: for Kosovo, local-language monitoring should be pointed at CBK/ATK/Kuvendi and think tanks, while firm alerts are monitored in English.
